summary: Manual design assessment passed. The node now treats Provision as a workflow-owned lifecycle surface, keeps ForgeLog responsible for widget-local timer cleanup, and narrows the follow-up to callable worker scheduling plus explicit teardown of bootstrap, disk-detect, flash, and post-flash watch boundaries.
checks: Research explains why Provision differs from aggregate refresh surfaces and why naive StyreneScreen resume refresh would replay bootstrap at the wrong workflow moments.
Decisions keep ProvisionScreen workflow-oriented, choose screen-local resource ownership plus callable worker scheduling, and preserve ForgeLog as the timer owner.
Acceptance criteria require cancellable bootstrap, callable scheduling for detect/flash work, and post-flash watch teardown that ends with the workflow.
Implementation notes keep the file scope narrow to Provision and only add forge-log or reticulum support changes if concrete cleanup needs require them.
